summary:
**Lunar Landing Site Navigator** is an interactive mission-planning platform designed to support the exploration and evaluation of potential lunar landing sites. The project aims to simplify complex lunar surface analysis by bringing essential mission-related information into a unified workspace. Users can explore candidate landing regions, inspect surrounding terrain, and compare locations based on important operational factors such as surface characteristics, solar illumination, and Earth visibility for communication.

The platform is inspired by NASA's Moon Trek, JPL Horizons System, and the Canadian Space Agency's Moon Exploration resources. By combining lunar terrain exploration with astronomical position calculations, the system aims to provide valuable insights into landing-site suitability, solar power availability, and communication opportunities.

Our goal is to develop an accessible, intuitive, and informative tool that helps students, researchers, and future mission planners understand the challenges of lunar exploration and make better-informed decisions for sustainable human and robotic missions to the Moon.
details:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator

Project Overview

Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive web-based mission-planning platform designed to help users explore, analyse, and compare potential landing locations on the Moon. It provides a unified workspace for understanding important factors that influence lunar landing-site selection and future surface missions.

How Does It Work?

The platform allows users to explore candidate lunar regions through an interactive interface, inspect geographical and terrain information, and evaluate locations based on mission-critical factors. These include surface characteristics, solar illumination, Sun positioning, Earth visibility, and potential communication opportunities.

The project takes inspiration from NASA's Moon Trek, JPL Horizons System, and the Canadian Space Agency's Moon Exploration resources. These resources provide the foundation for integrating lunar terrain exploration and astronomical calculations into the mission-planning workflow.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The platform aims to simplify complex lunar exploration information by presenting it through an accessible and intuitive interface. It can help students, researchers, and future mission planners better understand the challenges of selecting suitable landing regions.

Its intended impact is to support safer and more informed lunar mission planning, improve awareness of solar power availability and communication limitations, and encourage sustainable exploration of the Moon.

Tools and Technologies Used

The project was developed as a web-based application using:

  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the user interface and application functionality.
  • Google Antigravity as the AI-assisted development environment.
  • NASA Moon Trek for lunar terrain exploration and geographical reference.
  • JPL Horizons System for astronomical position and ephemeris data.
  • Canadian Space Agency Moon Exploration resources for mission-related research.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of this project is its mission-control-inspired interface, which brings different aspects of lunar exploration into one interactive environment. Instead of presenting disconnected scientific information, it aims to connect terrain exploration, astronomical positioning, power considerations, and communication visibility within a single workflow.

Factors Considered

During development, the team considered:

  • Lunar surface terrain and geographical conditions.
  • Sunlight availability for solar-powered operations.
  • Earth visibility and communication possibilities.
  • Accessibility and clarity of scientific information.
  • Reliability and accuracy of astronomical and geographical data.
  • Future scalability and integration of additional NASA datasets.

Ultimately, Lunar Landing Site Navigator aims to transform complex lunar exploration data into a more understandable and practical mission-planning experience.
